newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila says sugar imports swamp economic zones.
newsitem.headline: Manila says sugar imports swamp economic zones.

text.p: Duty-free imports of sugar in the country's economic zones exacerbated the country's sugar surplus, Customs Commissioner Guillermo Parayno said on Wednesday.
"We should not allow selling of sugar from special economic zones," Parayno told reporters.

Parayno said duty-free shops inside these export zones sold an estimated 13,000 tonnes of sugar to the outside market last year. Firms inside industrial estates are allowed tax- and duty-free imports.
There are 20 economic zones in the country, including the Subic and Clark freeports in central Luzon.
In October last year, the state-agency Sugar Regualtory Administration (SRA) suspended sugar imports up to March this year due to a glut.
The SRA said sugar imports from September 1995 to July 1996 reached 1.2 million tonnes.
Local raws dropped to a low of 500 pesos per 50-kilo bag late last year from 750 to 800 pesos at the start of 1996 due to the glut, sugar planters and millers said.
President Fidel Ramos has formed a multi-sectoral agency with representatives from the government, millers and planters to solve the crisis.
